maria: Quick sync — we ran head-to-head model comparisons yesterday but results look noisy. want to lock down a deterministic protocol so we can be confident perf deltas (kernel selection / batching / KV behavior).

maria: Summary of what I saw: p95 for model-A jumped ~30% between runs, model-B stayed stable. CPU/GPU util traces show different kernel picks at ~step 5. Also KV cache warmup seen on replay runs but not on synthetic.

alex: FWIW, we should ensure tokenizer alignment first — different tokenizers (or even different tokenization flags) will change decode length which wrecks throughput comparisons.

lee: +1. also need identical decode params (temp, top_p, max_new_tokens, stop sequences). I propose a checklist: same prompts file, same tokeniser binary + vocab hash, pinned decoding seeds, disable prefix caching for cold-start tests, and run warmup passes for steady-state numbers.

maria: I sketched a run command for the replay harness to use as a baseline:
```\n./replay-harness --models model-A,model-B \
  --prompts tests/head2head_prompts.json \
  --tokenizer-bin /opt/tokenizers/standard_tokenizer.bin \
  --decode "temperature=0.0,top_p=1.0,max_new_tokens=128,stop=[\"\n\"]" \
  --replay-mode exact-tokenization \
  --warmup 10 --samples 500 \
  --metric p50,p90,p95,throughput \
  --profile cpu,gpu,mem \
  --lock-kernel-selection \n```
(we use `--lock-kernel-selection` to force the runtime to use the same kernel family across both models during the run; useful to isolate batching/KV effects)

sarah: Nice. Two small asks: 1) capture KV cache hit-rate and cold-cache latencies per request. 2) include a run with continuous-batching enabled vs disabled, because our batching heuristics recently changed and could explain the p95 variance.

alex: On the kernel note: the runtime sometimes switches to smaller GEMM kernels when target seq_len > threshold. If model-A had slightly longer tokenization on the same prompts we might see a different kernel chosen. Pinning tokenization + kernel selection is important.

maria: Agreed. For apples-to-apples comparison we should also:
- export tokenizer hashes in the run metadata
- embed decode params in the log header
- add a reproducible RNG seed where applicable

lee: Perf-bot posted the last run artifacts: `perf-bot: artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/1718449000`

perf-bot: Latest artifacts for 1718449000: perf.log, profile.tar.gz, replay-trace.json, tokenizer-meta.json

maria: Thanks. @alex @lee can one of you re-run the harness with the exact command above but add `--kv-stats` and `--batching-mode off` and attach the `replay-trace.json`? aim: isolate whether KV warmup or batching heuristics cause the p95 spike.

alex: re-running now on the staging pool (gpus-rt-small). ETA ~20m. I'll post results and a condensed table.

lee: I'll also run a kernel-pinned variant: same command + `--force-kernel family=int8_fused` and compare.

maria: Perfect. After we have both runs, we'll diff: token counts, kernel switches, kv-hit curves, and per-request latency distribution. If we still see unexplained variance we'll run with: `--replay-mode synthetic` to validate whether the replay harness or real traces cause instability.

sarah: Quick note: when you post results include the small `perf-summary.csv` (we'll ingest into the benchdb) and a short note about any config differences. keeps dojo clean. :+1:

alex: Uploaded outputs: https://ci.internal/runs/1718454321/outputs.tar.gz — short summary: with batching off p95 stabilized for model-A, KV hit-rate still showed a ~12% warmup window on cold-starts. Detailed logs in `replay-trace.json`.

lee: Kernel-pinned run uploaded as well: https://ci.internal/runs/1718454321/kernel-pinned.tar.gz — No kernel switches observed, p95 diff narrowed to ~4%. Looks like heuristics + tokenization interplay was the main culprit.

maria: Great troubleshooting. Next steps: 1) formalize the run command in docs/bench-protocol.md, 2) add an automated check in the harness to fail runs that don't pin tokenizer hash + decode params, 3) file a small perf regression ticket for batching heuristics with the run artifacts attached. I'll create the ticket and assign to eng-runtime.

alex: thanks, will review the ticket and propose a small runtime patch (guardrail threshold for kernel switching).

maria: Thanks all. Closing once ticket created. :white_check_mark:
